summary: Staged rollout: health-check probe triggers routing drift to fallback during canary cutover
description: Issue summary: During a staged canary rollout for redwood-xl-v1 at NimblePay (dedicated cluster), periodic health-check probes from the routing plane caused a subset of sessions pinned to the new canary to be considered unhealthy and immediately redirected to fallback model variants. Impact: Customers observed unexpected model switching, degraded relevance for long-running chat sessions, and token duplication/partial-responses in streaming clients. This occurred during the third hour of a gradual 10%->50% rollout and coincided with a transient spike in probe failures from the new canary pool.
impact: ~12% of active user sessions across the NimblePay dedicated cluster experienced mid-session model switches and truncated streaming responses for ~27 minutes. Business impact: session-level quality regressions for chat support flows and two incident escalations to NimblePay SRE.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a staged rollout for redwood-xl-v1 -> redwood-xl-v1-quantized target at 10% traffic
2) Simulate increased health-check latency on a subset of canary serving nodes (add 200-500ms delay to probe handler),
3) Open long-running streaming chat sessions pinned to the canary variant and send ~3–5 progressive messages that exercise KV-cache hot paths
4) Observe routing decisions when the routing controller marks probes failed: sessions should remain pinned, but in this case they were routed to fallback variants immediately.
observed_behavior: Routing plane marked canary nodes unhealthy after 2 failed health probes and immediately evicted session affinity for ~48% of pinned sessions. Evicted sessions were routed to fallback model variants despite 'pin-preserve' policy being configured. Streaming clients received partial tokens and duplicate prefix tokens when the fallback resumed the completion mid-stream.
expected_behavior: With 'pin-preserve' and graceful-cutover enabled, in-flight pinned sessions should remain bound to their model instance until session end or until an explicit session eviction policy is met. Health-check probe flakiness should trigger degraded routing metrics but not instant session re-affinity until a safety window elapses.
root_cause_hypothesis: 1) Health-check controller uses per-node probe counters that treat transient latency as failures without respecting session-affinity override flags.
2) Routing controller's 'pin-preserve' check evaluates node liveness but not the explicit session pin metadata when a probe crosses the failure threshold, causing eviction races.
3) A recent change in health-check aggressive backoff logic (see PR #4876) reduced the failure window and inadvertently shortened the safe grace period for pinned sessions.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 13:35 UTC — Confirmed correlated spike in probe latency from canary pool nodes (quant-02/quant-03). Probe latency charts show 400-800ms p95 for 12m.
2026-03-10 13:45 UTC — Replayed router trace for sample session sn-77a2; router eviction occurred immediately after two consecutive probe timeouts, no extra safety window observed.
2026-03-10 14:10 UTC — Deployed temporary routing rule to honor session pin metadata (hotfix) for NimblePay cluster; observed cessation of mid-session evictions within 3 minutes of rule rollout.
2026-03-10 15:00 UTC — Cross-checked PR #4876 against canary: matches behavioral change in health-check backoff config.
current_workaround: Applied cluster-scoped routing override to honor session pins (hotfix) and increased the health-check failure threshold for canary nodes from 2->5 probes. Workaround mitigated evictions for affected customer within 10 minutes but increases detection latency for truly unhealthy nodes.
proposed_fix: 1) Revert aggressive backoff change in health-check controller for pinned-session rollout groups (PR rollback or config patch). 2) Add an explicit 'pin-safe-window' check in the routing controller: if session has pin metadata and session age < X hours, do not evict for probe failures unless node reports terminal fatal state. 3) Add integration test that simulates probe latency to validate session-affinity guarantees.
priority_next_steps: a) Schedule config rollback for health-check backoff in next maintenance window (owner: infra-platform).
b) Implement routing controller 'pin-safe-window' guard and unit tests (owner: routing-team).
c) Update canary runbook to include probe-latency thresholds and safe grace period guidance (owner: SRE).
d) Post-incident review with NimblePay and share mitigation timeline and follow-ups.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied (routing override + increased probe threshold). Full fix postponed pending routing controller change and tests. Customer notified and postmortem scheduled.
resolution_notes: Hotfix timeline: 2026-03-10 14:12 UTC routing override applied, 14:22 UTC probe threshold increased, evictions stopped by 14:35 UTC.
Rollback plan: revert health-check backoff PR from main to stable branch after validation in staging. Expected deploy: 2026-03-15.
Customer communication: Support provided a technical summary and temporary mitigation details to NimblePay account team; customer requested timeline for permanent fix.
